description: Fideo Seco is a cherished Mexican dry noodle dish, offering a comforting and rich tomato-based flavor profile. Tiny, toasted noodles absorb a savory sauce, creating a deeply satisfying meal that's perfect on its own or as a side. This traditional recipe brings the warmth and heart of Mexican home cooking to your table.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: In a blender, combine the roughly chopped tomatoes, onion, and garlic cloves with 1/2 cup of the chicken broth. Blend until completely smooth. If using, add the tomato paste to the blender for a richer color and flavor. Set aside.

instructions.title: Toast the Fideo Noodles
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or a shallow pot over medium heat. Add the fideo noodles and stir constantly until they are evenly golden brown. This step is crucial for flavor and prevents the noodles from becoming mushy. Be careful not to burn them.

instructions.title: Add the Sauce and Simmer
instructions.text: Carefully pour the blended tomato sauce into the skillet with the toasted fideo noodles. Stir well to ensure all the noodles are coated. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.

instructions.title: Add Broth and Season
instructions.text: Pour in the remaining 1 1/2 cups of chicken broth. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir everything together, then reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let it simmer for about 10-12 minutes, or until most of the liquid has been absorbed by the noodles.

instructions.title: Rest and Fluff
instructions.text: Once the liquid is mostly absorbed and the noodles are tender, remove the skillet from the heat. Keep it covered and let the Fideo Seco rest for 5 minutes. This allows the remaining liquid to fully absorb and the flavors to meld. Gently fluff the noodles with a fork before serving.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Serve the Fideo Seco warm, garnished generously with crumbled queso fresco, fresh chopped cilantro, and a dollop of Mexican crema or sour cream. It makes a wonderful main course or a flavorful side dish.

tips: Toasting the fideo noodles evenly until golden brown is the most important step for achieving a rich flavor and preventing stickiness. Do not rush this process.
For a vegetarian version, simply substitute chicken broth with vegetable broth. You can also add a pinch of cumin to the sauce for an extra layer of authentic flavor.
Fideo Seco is excellent served immediately, but leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of broth if needed.
